settings.title: Settings
settings.language.help: Applies immediately: UI text, tray menu and the automatic font (theme font_name = "auto") all switch. Item names and aliases are data and stay unchanged.
settings.general.sendto_label: Right-click a file/folder → Send to → egui-launcher
settings.general.sendto_help: On = writes egui-launcher.lnk into the SendTo folder; off = deletes it (only the file this program created; a same-named file owned by someone else is left alone).
settings.general.autostart_label: Start silently at sign-in (tray only, no window)
settings.general.autostart_help: On = writes egui-launcher.lnk into the Startup folder with the -Startup argument (no window after sign-in); off = deletes it (only the file this program created whose arguments are exactly -Startup). Off by default.
settings.general.space.off: Only when the box is empty
settings.general.space.help:
Only on the full name (default) = Space runs when the whole query exactly equals the highlighted item's name, or one of its aliases (jsb→Notepad, Task Scheduler→itself). For a mere prefix (tas, task sch) Space still types a space; to commit, press Tab to complete and then Space, or just press Enter.
Only when one result = Space runs as soon as the filter narrows to a single row; the cost is that a space inside a “unique but not finished” query needs Shift+Space.
Only when the box is empty = the most conservative: spaces in multi-word queries are untouched and one-handed use still needs Enter.
Always = Space is always a confirm; the cost is that you cannot type a space in a query.
Shift+Space means “type a real space” in all four modes.
settings.general.tab.help:
Complete first = Tab completes the whole word only when exactly one candidate can be extended by this query (e.g. jsq→Calculator); more than one candidate means the ambiguity is unresolved, so Tab cycles to the next item instead and never guesses the first one for you.
Navigation only = Tab next, Shift+Tab previous (what the Delphi ALTRun does); the cost is no completion.
Both modes keep ↑↓ paging and PgUp/PgDn; Tab navigation wraps at the ends while ↑↓ stays clamped. For stable navigation that completion can never steal, use Ctrl+N / Ctrl+P (or Ctrl+J / Ctrl+K).
settings.general.rank_title: Learning order within a match tier
settings.general.rank.help:
This layer only orders items whose match tier is the same; the better-matching one is always first.
Count first (default) = more runs come first, and only equal counts look at the last use. Something used once does not push down an old favourite used dozens of times.
Count + time decay = compares log2(1+count) × 0.5^(days since last use / 7). Counts still carry weight but log2 compresses the magnitude, and an item's heat halves after a full week unused, so “used once last week” won't linger at the top.
Pin (Ctrl+Shift+P) always overrides this layer; use it to nail down an item instead of working around it with a mode.
settings.general.rows_title: Rows shown in the main list
settings.general.rows.help:
All (default) = every result goes into the list; the window is still ten rows tall, so scroll for the rest. This matches the Delphi ALTRun, where “10 rows” was only the list height and results were never truncated.
10 rows = the list shows the first 10 lines only, and hint rows such as calculator / web search take a slot too; the window is already ten rows tall, so no scrolling is needed.
Both modes affect display and how far the keyboard can reach; truncated items are not unmatched, switch to All to see them immediately (or make the query more precise).
settings.general.density.help:
A · Snug (default) = row 34 / icon 24 / gap 2 ⇒ window height 438.
B · Roomy = 40 / 28 / 2 ⇒ 498. C · Ultra-dense = 24 / 16 / 0 ⇒ 318.
Follow theme = row height and icon size go back to the theme's `row_height` / `icon_size` (Light 54/32, Compact 44/26, Modern 56/32) and the window grows accordingly.
All four modes keep “exactly ten rows on screen”: switching only changes row height, the window height is recomputed from it, the width is untouched.
Those totals assume the Light padding of 14; another theme only shifts by those few pixels; the input row is unaffected (fixed height 44, its font still follows the theme's input font size).
The reference points are the two older versions — the Delphi one used row height 16 without icons (plain text can be that tight), the AHK one used 54 with zero gap and a 700-wide window (its airiness came from width, not row height). This one has icons and is 500 wide, so the middle mode is the default.
Note: outside “Follow theme”, the theme JSON keys `row_height` and `icon_size` are not used for rendering (the other 22 keys still apply).
settings.general.scope.help:
All (default) = every item in the list is shown as before.
Basic = only the built-in whitelist (Calculator, Notepad, Shutdown and other common commands) plus items you added yourself; the big pile of maintenance tools (Device Manager, Registry Editor, 36 Settings pages …) stays out of the list.
You can pull categories in on the fly with @category: type @maintenance to list the whole maintenance category, @maintenance disk to search “disk” inside it, @basic for the whitelist only. An explicit @ ignores this setting.
Ctrl+G cycles this setting from the main window.
An item's own categories are edited in the “Category” box of the add/edit dialog (comma- or space-separated, multiple allowed).
settings.general.dups.help: On a collision only the first item in the list wins; learned aliases are counted in this table too (a duplicate does not block use).
settings.general.seeds.none: No built-in command is missing; the list was not touched
settings.general.seeds.added_hidden: ✓ Restored {1} item(s) ({2} hidden again by hidden[])
settings.general.seeds.help: Only missing ones are added (matched by uid / name), nothing is deleted and edited items are left alone. A deleted built-in does not come back on its own at the next start; use this button to get it back. Items listed in settings.json's hidden array are removed again after being restored (hidden ≠ deleted).
settings.general.history.help:
Remember the last {1}: every run (Enter to launch, clicking a file row, a terminal command starting with >, copying from the calculator, picking a row in the action panel) stores the query text in search_history.json. Ctrl+↑ goes further back, Ctrl+↓ forward; pressing Ctrl+↓ once more at the newest returns to what you typed yourself.
Only text is stored, never results: a recalled string never launches anything by itself, Enter still runs it. Duplicates match case-insensitively (C:\Foo and c:\foo are the same) but are stored as typed.
0 = stop recording; the next run also clears the existing entries and saves. To wipe them now without changing the limit, use “Clear search history” on the Advanced page.
Text in this table only goes to search_history.json, never to launcher.log.
status.panel: Actions · Esc or ← back to results
hud.need_close_windows: Close the launcher's dialog or settings first, then press the selection hotkey again
hud.pasted_chars: ✓ Pasted {1} characters into the previous window
manage.title: Batch manage
manage.help:
Tick any items, then convert paths or delete them. Deleting only removes entries from the list, never files on disk.
The state column uses the four states from the main screen: `-` = not checked (URLs / built-in actions / anything containing {query}), `Offline` = drive or network location unreachable (unplugged USB stick, dropped share) — that is not "file not found", and "select broken only" will not tick it.
manage.select_broken_hover: Ticks only "Not found" rows; Offline does not count — the medium is absent, the entry itself is fine
manage.recheck_hover: Runs the four-state check again; a disconnected network drive may take a few seconds
manage.empty: The list is empty: press Ctrl+Shift+N on the main screen to create one, or Ctrl+I to batch import.
manage.to_relative_hover: Rewrites absolute paths under {1} as {2}\…; arguments and working directory stay untouched
manage.to_absolute_hover: Turns %LAUNCHER_DIR%\… or .\… back into an absolute path under this program folder
manage.delete_hover: Removes these entries from the list only, without deleting files on disk
manage.reason_not_under: (not under this program folder, or already relative)
usage.title: Usage statistics
usage.help: Counts only: which kind of feature, which day, how many times. Query text, item names and paths never enter usage.json or launcher.log.
usage.retention: Keeps {1} days: the earliest record kept is {2}, and anything older is trimmed on every write (this is "{3} days back from today", not "keep the latest {4} entries").
usage.empty: No records yet: run a list item, an expression, a web search or a file row and numbers will appear here.
usage.unknown: Other (buckets this version does not know) {1} times — counted in the total but not in the buckets above
usage.dual_count: One launch can land in two buckets: custom commands in the list count as both "list item" and "custom command" (the former = this entry was launched, the latter = a custom command was run) ⇒ the total can exceed the actual number of launches. That is intentional, not double counting.
usage.top_empty: No list item has been launched successfully yet.
usage.top_note: This counts list items themselves (deleting an item removes it here) and is separate from the per-feature ledger above.
usage.clear_help:
Turns usage.json into an empty table: total, the last-30-day bars and "count by feature" all go to zero.
Per-item use counts and last-used times stay — that is a separate ledger used for ranking; to clear it use "Reset learning order" on the Advanced page. No backup for this one.
web.title: Web search engines
web.help: "keyword + space + term" takes over the whole list (e.g. g weather). In the URL template {query} is replaced by the term and {query|8000} is the default when the term is empty; a template with no placeholder at all is just a bookmark. A keyword only takes over on an exact first-word match (case-insensitive); a partial word (goo) does not count.
web.icon_hover: The icon at the far left of the search row
web.icon_hint: Icon (empty = the system default for the URL)
web.download_hover: Fetches an icon for this row's URL, saves it under Icons\ and fills the path on the left
web.incomplete_row: {1} rows are missing a keyword or URL
web.dirty_note: {1} — not saved when you leave this page (only the first of duplicates is kept).
web.foot_help: Edit a field and click elsewhere to save. "Restore the nine factory engines" replaces the whole table, wiping your own entries. An empty icon means the system default for the URL; "Download icon" fetches one from the site and stores it under Icons\ in the data folder, filling the relative path on the left. Downloads need network and run one at a time.
web.fallback_help: When there are no results, the list ends with search rows from this sequence. Factory = Google → Bing (engines missing from the table are skipped). Pick one engine to show only its row.
web.fallback_deleted: Deleted engine (reverts to factory when you leave this page)
settings.features.import_help: Scans Start menu / desktop shortcuts into the list (existing entries are neither duplicated nor removed).
settings.features.confirm_label: Confirm before shutdown / restart / sign out / empty Recycle Bin (on by default)
settings.features.confirm_help: When off, those four run on Enter right from the list. They are all irreversible; only turn this off if you are sure you will not press them by mistake.
settings.features.syscmd_help: System commands (shutdown, settings shortcuts, Windows tools, ms-settings pages, volume and media) join the built-in items and can be searched, pinned, edited and deleted like any other entry. To hide rather than delete, clear the query box on the main screen, select an item and press Ctrl+Del (hidden items stay hidden even after "restore missing built-in commands"); restore them on the Advanced page.
settings.features.shell_help:
Typing `>command` in the query box (e.g. `>ipconfig /all`) runs it in a new window that stays open so you can read the output; typing only `>` shows usage rows.
cmd / powershell / pwsh each open a new console window; the Windows Terminal option hands the same command to a new tab (via cmd). Changes apply immediately, no restart. The raw command never enters the log.
sources.title: Enabled data sources
sources.help: A source that is off neither searches nor shows hint rows, and stays off on the next start (the switch lives in settings.json's sources_off). Changes apply immediately, no restart.
common.press_new_combo: Press the new combo… (Esc / Tab cancels, Backspace / Delete restores default)
hotkeys.toggle_help:
Click "Record new hotkey" and press the combo you want — no confirmation needed: a successful registration takes effect at once and is written to settings.json; if the system or another program owns it, the error is reported and the previous combo is restored (your old setting is not lost).
Recordable keys: letters, digits, space, Enter, the backtick ` and F1–F24. Non-F keys need Ctrl, Alt or Win, because a bare A or Shift+A is just typing — as a global key it would intercept all your input.
The only bare key allowed is ` (batch R, added 2026-10-20 at your request): the price is that after setting it nothing system-wide can type a `, so pair it with the escape hatch on the "Typeback hotkey" card below; the ~ from Shift+` is unaffected (measured on this machine). While recording, the program temporarily unregisters the current global hotkey — otherwise the system would swallow a bare ` entirely and the program would receive no key at all, making it impossible to record; recording ends (settled / Esc / cancel button / closing the window / hiding to tray) and the hotkey is reinstalled immediately, with a 30-second fallback timer so it can never stay unregistered.
Win combos cannot be recorded here: on Windows egui does not pass Win as a modifier (when you press Ctrl, the command bit it reports is a copy of Ctrl). For Win+X use the checkboxes on the typeback card below.
The program's own combos (Ctrl+N/E/D/I/J/K/M/L/B/R, Ctrl+Shift+N/D/P, Ctrl+digit, Alt+digit, F1–F4, Alt+Enter) are blocked locally first; this list is not exhaustive — trust the message you get when something is actually blocked. Global ownership can only be found by "trying to register" — Windows has no API to enumerate other programs' hotkeys, so "no error" only means the system allows it right now, not that nobody else on the machine wants the key.
One more thing: global hotkeys are swallowed by the system as a whole, so setting something like Ctrl+A or Ctrl+C removes that action from every other program (this program does not bind them, so it will not stop you here — avoid them yourself).
hotkeys.extra_none: ℹ There never was a secondary hotkey
hotkeys.extra_help:
Ships as Alt+R and works like your main hotkey above: one press toggles show/hide (this is the AHK build's "secondary hotkey").
Same rules as the main hotkey: a modifier is required, and it must not equal the main or typeback hotkey; settings.json is written only after a successful registration, and a failure reports the error and reinstalls the previous one. After "Clear" only the main summon key remains; "Restore default" brings it back.
hotkeys.selection_title: Selection hotkey (grab the foreground window's selection and open the action panel)
hotkeys.selection_none: ℹ There never was a selection hotkey
hotkeys.selection_help:
Ships as Ctrl+Alt+\ (your ruling, 2026-10-30). Select some text / a URL / some files in any program and press it: the program briefly presses Ctrl+C for you (Ctrl+Insert in console windows), classifies the result as "file / URL / text" and opens the usual action panel — so actions like "open in browser", "copy path" or "open containing folder" work on the selection too.
The keystroke it sends never damages your clipboard: before pressing it snapshots every clipboard format and puts it back verbatim right after (images and non-text content included); if the snapshot fails it abandons the attempt and touches nothing.
A modifier is required and it must not equal the other three hotkeys; settings.json is written only after a successful registration. After "Clear" this program no longer holds the key.
hotkeys.tap_title: Double-tap summon (tap the same modifier twice)
hotkeys.tap_help:
Tapping the same modifier twice toggles show/hide (left and right Ctrl / Shift both count, and the two taps may be different sides).
Rules: the two taps must be within 400ms; holding one down for over 300ms does not count (that is the start of a combo such as Ctrl+C); if the gap between releases is under 25ms it is discarded as remote-control / automation jitter. Shift+CapsLock and other modifier-then-key presses work as usual and are not taken as a double tap.
Off by default. When on, the program installs a listen-only keyboard hook: every key still reaches the program you are using, and the hook only counts the two taps.
hotkeys.typeback_title: Typeback hotkey (press it to type the character swallowed by the summon key)
hotkeys.typeback_needkey: ⚠ Typeback hotkey: click the field on the left first, then press a key
hotkeys.typeback_none: ℹ There never was a typeback hotkey
hotkeys.typeback.state_muted: ○ Currently {1}, but the summon key {2} has a modifier and swallows no character ⇒ pressing it produces nothing (only useful with a bare summon key).
hotkeys.typeback.state_ok: ✓ Currently {1}: pressing it types {2} into the focused window.
hotkeys.typeback.state_novk: ⚠ Currently {1}, but the summon key's VK maps to no character in the current keyboard layout (a bare F key is like this), so pressing it produces nothing.
hotkeys.typeback.state_failed: ⚠ Set to {1}, but registration failed this time, so it does nothing.
hotkeys.typeback_help:
Why it exists: once the summon key is a bare `, that character can no longer be typed anywhere system-wide (the ~ from Shift+` is unaffected), and this card is the escape hatch. When the summon key has a modifier (the factory Ctrl+Alt+Space does), it swallows nothing ⇒ this key does nothing, so it never stuffs a stray space into what you are typing.
The character is not hard-coded: it is derived from the summon key's VK and the current keyboard layout (MapVirtualKeyW), so changing layouts does not type the wrong key.
A modifier is required (any of Ctrl / Alt / Win): a bare key would just replace the swallowing key with itself. It must also not equal the summon key — the system would treat it as the summon key. Win+` is recommended: the Win bit can only be set by the checkboxes here, and Win+` is usually unclaimed.
One thing not yet measured: injection goes through SendInput's Unicode channel (no VK, so the program's own bare ` cannot swallow it again); real behavior in Notepad / browsers / VS Code / terminals / IMEs still needs hands-on acceptance.
hotkeys.secondary_title: Secondary action key (press it with a row selected)
hotkeys.secondary_help:
"Shortcut mode" = pressing {1} does one thing directly: locate a file / folder row in Explorer, copy a web search row's URL, paste a calculator / text row into the previous window (since batch E5 on 2026-10-27; this path needs the "previous window" recorded at summon time, and refuses with an explanation rather than pretending when it was not); "panel mode" = same as →, opens the action panel and you pick there.
App items, system commands and custom commands have no obvious secondary action — shortcut mode tells you to press → for the full list instead of guessing (Enter already opens them; a second alias would only make two keys fight over the same thing).
This key only works on the search page with no dialog or panel open, and it is not registered with the system: it never steals keys from other programs and is never swallowed system-wide like a global hotkey. It must include Ctrl or Alt (bare keys and Shift-only keys are just typing), and Win combos cannot be set (egui does not pass Win on Windows).
Changes take effect immediately and write straight to settings.json — the system does not hold this key, so there is no "try to register" step and no "owned by another program" case.
hotkeys.grid.toggle: Summon / hide globally (change it in the card above)
hotkeys.grid.extra: Secondary summon: a second summon key with the same effect (edit or clear it in the card above; batch G1)
hotkeys.grid.tap: Double-tap summon: tap Ctrl or Shift twice to toggle (change it in the card above; off by default)
hotkeys.grid.secondary: Secondary action: shortcut mode does one thing directly (locate a file row / copy a web row's URL / paste a text row into the previous window); panel mode equals → (change it in the card above)
hotkeys.grid.typeback: Typeback: types the character swallowed by the summon key into the focused window (change it in the card above)
hotkeys.grid.history: Browse search history: older / newer; press Ctrl+↓ again at the newest to return to what you typed (batch C3; the limit lives under "Search history" on the General page; does not take over in panel or file mode)
hotkeys.grid.pgup: Page the result list (scrolling follows the selection)
hotkeys.grid.num: Run row 1–9 / row 10 (the first 10 rows are numbered); the bare keys work only when the input is empty, Ctrl+digit / Alt+digit always work
hotkeys.grid.tab: Complete / next item (per "Tab key behavior" on the settings page); in complete-first mode Tab completes only when exactly one candidate can be extended by the query, otherwise it navigates; a selected folder row always enters that folder (FR-SRC-14)
hotkeys.grid.shift_tab: Previous item (same in both Tab modes)
hotkeys.grid.ctrl_np: Next / previous item (always navigation, never taken over by completion)
hotkeys.grid.ctrl_jk: Same, another pair (kept for old habits)
hotkeys.grid.space: Run the selected item (by default only when the input is empty; change it under "Run on space" on the settings page)
hotkeys.grid.drag_edge: Resize the window (6px invisible handles on four edges + four corners, minimum 360×240)
hotkeys.grid.zoom: Grow / shrink the window one step (60×40 logical pixels; same as the keyboard path above)
hotkeys.grid.drag_move: Move the window: empty title-bar space (between the search box and ☰, right of the settings title) or empty space right of the list; the middle button no longer runs items
hotkeys.grid.menu: Main menu: new, batch import, settings, cheatsheet, open log, exit (replaces the old "＋ New" button since batch F6)
hotkeys.grid.enter: Run the selected item; confirm in a dialog / confirmation; add-new when nothing matches
hotkeys.grid.esc: Close ☰ menu → close confirmation → close dialog → back from settings → clear input → hide to tray (in order)
hotkeys.grid.new: New shortcut (prefilled with the path and type when a file row is selected)
hotkeys.grid.edit: Edit the selected item (F3 is an alias added in batch B8, same path; neither takes over while the panel is open)
hotkeys.grid.delete: Delete the selected item (only when the input is empty; asks for confirmation)
hotkeys.grid.delete_any: Delete the selected item (no input restriction; asks for confirmation)
hotkeys.grid.open_dir: Open the selected item's folder (file rows: reveal the file in Explorer)
hotkeys.grid.pin: Pin / unpin the selected item (badge at the icon's top-right)
hotkeys.grid.file_mode: Enter file mode: prepends a ' trigger to the input; already in file mode it only hints and adds no second prefix
hotkeys.grid.cheatsheet: Open the cheatsheet: all syntax and shortcuts on one page (`? word` filters, Enter opens an entry's help page)
hotkeys.grid.fs_path: File mode #1: type a path to browse that level (a trailing separator lists the whole folder; without one it is "folder + filter")
hotkeys.grid.fs_quote: #2: search file names within the index scope (Desktop / Downloads / Documents, up to four levels, capped at 30k entries)
hotkeys.grid.fs_type: #4: filter by extension type (folders are not type-filtered)
hotkeys.grid.fs_space: #6: a leading space enters file mode (the real space inserted with Shift+space)
hotkeys.grid.file_ctx: Copy path / show in Explorer / add as shortcut (a file row is not in the list ⇒ edit, delete and pin do not apply)
hotkeys.grid.settings: Open / return from settings (F2 is an alias added in batch B8; both work on the settings page too)
hotkeys.grid.about: About: version, program location, item count (Esc closes; batch B8)
hotkeys.grid.config_dir: Open the config folder (settings.json / user_items.json / launcher.log all live there; batch B8)
hotkeys.grid.copy_row: Copy the current row: path for files, number for the calculator, name for apps and commands (batch B8); a selection in the input box is copied first; does not close the window
hotkeys.grid.wheel: One wheel notch on the result list selects the previous/next row, clamped at both ends without wrapping; scroll position still follows the selection (batch B8)
files.folder_hover: Supports %ENVVARS%; a row whose folder does not exist is skipped
files.folder_help: Edits apply when you click elsewhere (leave the field); adding/removing applies at once. The index is then rebuilt in the background, and the old one stays usable until it is done, so the UI never stalls. Rows whose folder does not exist are skipped.
files.exclude_help: Excluded names skip the whole folder (case-insensitive), and files beneath it stay out of the index. "Restore default exclusions" writes the seven factory entries back (node_modules / .git and so on) — your own entries are wiped, and anything removed by mistake can be added again.
files.tiers_help: "(default)" marks the factory tier. Values set by hand in settings.json outside the tiers still apply; no tier is selected in the UI, and clicking any tier overrides it. Min length is the threshold for entering file mode ('word / leading space) and has nothing to do with normal search.
appearance.remember_position: Remember window position (return there on next summon)
appearance.status_bar: Show the bottom status bar (38px, only when there are results)
appearance.fade: Fade in on summon (120ms, cubic ease-out)
appearance.help: Width range 360–900 (default 500). No fade-out: the spec asks for a shadow window, and fading before hiding would violate "hiding must not block the next hotkey summon" in the same clause.
appearance.override_note: Currently an appearance-page override; the theme value is still there — click the button to hand it back.
appearance.following_note: Following the theme ({1}). Edit opacity in the theme JSON, or drag the slider above.
appearance.theme_help: 19 built in plus "Follow system". User themes go in the Themes folder next to the exe (falling back to %LOCALAPPDATA%\egui-launcher\Themes when not writable); the file name is the theme name, and a same-name file overrides the built-in. Theme changes apply without a restart; files edited while hidden are re-read on the next summon.
appearance.export_disabled: "Follow system" has no single palette; pick a concrete theme in the gallery first
appearance.summary_metrics: row {1} | icon {2} | padding {3} | selected radius {4} | opacity {5} ({6}/255 ≈ {7}%, {8})
appearance.density_note: (Row density is "{1}", so row height and icons do not use the two numbers above — switch "List row density" on the General page to "Follow theme" to make them count. Padding still applies.)
appearance.color_help: Colors and the remaining sizes live in the theme JSON (24 keys, see spec 6.2); colors are written RRGGBB, and a bad key keeps its inherited value with one line in the log. Opacity can also be overridden with the slider above; "Follow theme" hands it back.
advanced.update_help: Asks GitHub for the latest release once. Read-only: nothing on disk changes, and a newer version only gives you a link to its download page — the launcher never downloads or replaces itself.
advanced.log_help:
Currently active: {1} ({2}). The log goes to launcher.log; ☰ → "Open log" shows it.
"Standard" records one-off conclusions only: startup, config, hotkeys, actions. "Verbose" also adds the per-frame perf line "perf: label milliseconds" and per-search / per-index details. Neither records the raw text you type, window titles or directory paths.
When this is blank (follow build), debug builds log Verbose and release builds log Standard — chatty in dev, quiet in release.
advanced.log_follow_build_hint: Chosen by build: debug = Verbose, release = Standard (this build picks "{1}")
advanced.sysinfo_help: Puts version / OS / renderer / DPI / appearance / storage locations / item counts / hotkeys into the clipboard as plain text — paste the whole thing when reporting an issue. C:\Users\<user> in paths becomes %USERPROFILE%; item names, raw queries and window titles are never included. The tray menu has the same entry.
advanced.reset_learning_help:
Clears every item's use count / last-used time so ranking returns to an unboosted state; pins (Ctrl+Shift+P) are unaffected. user_items.json is backed up first.
Aliases learned on submit cannot be cleared — they live in the same slot as aliases you type by hand and cannot be told apart afterwards (known deviation of FR-ACT-10).
advanced.clear_history_help:
Stored: {1} entries (limit {2}). Clearing turns search_history.json into an empty table and Ctrl+↑ starts from empty; the limit on the General page is unaffected.
No backup for this one: the two buttons above both back up first because they clear statistics; this table holds the raw text you typed, and keeping a copy would be the exact opposite of "clear". To stop recording altogether, set the limit to 0.
advanced.clear_params_empty: Nothing stored yet: once you type values into a parameterized item's parameter box, there will be something to clear here.
advanced.clear_params_help:
Stored: {1} entries (limit {2}; newest first, reuse only bumps the count without reordering).
This is the "recently used parameters" list under the parameter box; after clearing you have to retype them one by one.
No backup here either: it clears the raw text you typed.
advanced.restore_help:
Restores factory values for space-to-run / Tab semantics / learning rank / data source switches / dangerous-action confirmation / terminal shell / theme / displayed rows / row density / default scope, after writing a settings.json backup.
Kept: global hotkeys, typeback hotkey, web engines, hidden items, the built-in reseed round, plus custom commands, pins, usage counts and category tags in user_items.json.
advanced.hidden_empty: No hidden items. Clear the query box on the main screen, select an item and press Ctrl+Del to hide it — built-in commands, scanned items and custom items all work.
advanced.hidden_help: Hiding is not deleting: the item stays out of the list, and neither rescanning nor "restore missing built-in commands" brings it back. Restoring also brings back its pin and usage counts.
toast.manage_none_broken: No broken items found (Offline is not broken)
toast.manage_busy: The previous check has not returned yet, hold on
toast.manage_convert_none: None of the {1} selected items can be converted{2}
cheat.help.title: Cheat sheet (this page)
cheat.help.summary: `? word` shows only the entries containing that word
cheat.help.detail:
Type `?` to list every syntax rule and shortcut; `? file`, `? shortcut`, `? terminal` keep only the related entries.
↑↓ picks one, Enter or a click opens its help page; Esc closes.
Only character 0 of the query counts — a ` ?` with a leading space does not. This page lists only the syntax of the data sources that are currently on.
cheat.web.title: Web search
cheat.web.summary: `engine keyword word` takes over the whole list
cheat.web.detail:
Nine ship from the factory: `g` Google, `bing` Bing, `bd` Baidu, `gh` GitHub, `wiki` Wikipedia, `yt` YouTube, `tb` Taobao, `jd` JD, `tr` Google Translate.
Add, edit or delete engines under “Web engines” on the Settings page (page 10, `Ctrl+W`); you can still edit settings.json's
`web_engines` directly (including the URL template, where `{query}` is replaced).
A keyword typed in full without a following space is still an ordinary search; only a space plus a word takes over. When there is not a single result, rows from the fallback sequence appear (factory google → bing, changeable).
cheat.custom_args.title: Custom commands (parameters required)
cheat.custom_args.summary: Commands marked “parameters required” in the item list
cheat.custom_args.detail:
`keyword arguments` takes over the whole list, and `{query}` in the command line is replaced by the arguments.
When the keyword is complete but the arguments are still missing, the head rows show one hint line first; Enter fills in “keyword + space”.
The arguments are part of the query string: the log records only the command name, never the arguments.
cheat.query_placeholder.title: Parameter placeholder
cheat.query_placeholder.summary: That one slot in a custom command's command line
cheat.query_placeholder.detail:
Write the command line as `ping {query}`; typing `ping example.com` substitutes the whole segment; it may appear several times.
A command without `{query}` that receives extra arguments runs with its original arguments.
To edit a command: select that row in the item list and press Ctrl+E.
cheat.param_markers.title: Parameter markers
cheat.param_markers.summary: Stand-ins inside the command line / parameters, valued at the moment of summon; replaced only when encoding is not “no parameters”
cheat.param_markers.detail:
Five markers: `{%p}` the parameters you typed · `{%c}` the clipboard text at the moment of summon · `{%wd}` the foreground window handle (decimal) · `{%wt}` its title · `{%wc}` its window class name.
They are replaced only when “Encoding” in the edit dialog is not “no parameters”; with encoding = no parameters they go to the program as they are.
If markers are present but “no parameters” is left in place, you get asked once when saving.
Four encoding tiers: no parameters = launch directly; parameters not encoded = substituted as-is; URL encoding = spaces become `+`, Chinese becomes UTF-8 percent-escapes; UTF-8 encoding follows the same rules as URL encoding (kept only to recognize old Delphi configs).
Entries whose encoding is not “no parameters” show a `*` before the name in the list row.
The three window markers take the foreground window from before the summon, not this program; “Test run” in the dialog treats `{%p}` as empty and expands the other markers from the current scene.
cheat.runflags.title: Run flags
cheat.runflags.summary: One flag at the start/end of the command line changes the state the target window opens in
cheat.runflags.detail:
`@+` maximize · `@-` minimize · `@` hidden (starts in the background, no window).
Accepted at the “end” of the command line (`notepad.exe@`, as the requirement spec writes it) or at the “start” (`@notepad.exe`, the Delphi way); only one is honored per command, and when both ends carry one the leading flag decides.
It only applies on this program's own launch path; URLs ignore it (the browser opens its own window).
It has no effect when the target program itself ignores the initial display state the system passes in — Notepad and cmd do honor it.
cheat.calc.title: Calculator
cheat.calc.summary: Adds one head row when the text evaluates to a number
cheat.calc.detail:
The four operators, parentheses and exponentiation (`^`), units allowed. A leading `=` is the explicit way of saying “this is an expression”; it is optional.
A whole string that is just one number produces no row (otherwise row 0 would always be the calculator, and the number keys would all turn into copying digits).
Enter puts only the plain number on the clipboard (no thousands separators, no units).
cheat.units.title: Unit conversion
cheat.units.detail:
Eight categories: length, area, volume, mass, temperature, speed, time, data (temperature is written like `100C to F`).
You can also compute directly: `2 h + 30 min`, `1 day + 7`.
A bare number keeps the unit on the left: `1 day + 7` is 8 days, not 8 days 7 seconds. The subtitle of a conversion result states the direction.
cheat.radix_date.title: Radix conversion and date arithmetic
cheat.radix_date.detail:
When the whole string is just one radix literal (`0x1F`, `0b1010`, `0o17`), the subtitle gives the value in the other radixes.
Date words: `today` / `now` / `tomorrow` / `yesterday`; `today + 7 days` yields a date, `2026-12-25 - today` yields the number of days between.
cheat.match_modes.title: List matching: pinyin / camel case / multiple words
cheat.match_modes.summary: Chinese names match by pinyin initials, English names by camel-case initials
cheat.match_modes.detail:
Pinyin initials: `jsb` hits “Notepad” (only Chinese titles, such as apps and custom commands, have them).
Camel case / word initials: `vsc` hits Visual Studio Code.
A multi-word query is split on spaces and every word must match for a row to count (`report 2026`); word order does not matter.
cheat.wildcard.title: Wildcards / regex
cheat.wildcard.summary: `*` any run of characters, `?` a single character; everything else is interpreted as regex
cheat.wildcard.detail:
When `*` or `?` appears in the query, the whole string is treated as one regex: `*` → `.*`, `?` → `.`, and the other characters go to the regex engine as they are (so `^` `$` `\d` `[a-z]` work too).
Examples: `*calc` finds names containing calc; `c?lc` requires exactly one character in the middle; `*.exe` looks only at executables.
Everything is compared in lowercase (the same rule as the Delphi version), so an uppercase class escape such as `\D` becomes `\d`.
A malformed regex (e.g. `*[`) neither errors nor interrupts; the whole round falls back to ordinary matching.
A wildcard query no longer uses the pinyin-initial / subsequence tiers and is not split into words — the whole string is one pattern.
Note that `?` at character 0 is the cheat sheet entry; to match a single character put it later (`c?lc`).
cheat.tags.title: Category filter
cheat.tags.summary: `@category word` lists only that category; several categories are unioned
cheat.tags.detail:
An entry's “Category” tags are edited in the “Category” field of the add/edit dialog, comma- or space-separated, several allowed.
Typing `@maintenance` lists only entries with that tag, and a word can follow (`@maintenance disk` filters further inside the maintenance category).
`@maintenance @development disk` is a union: entries of both categories enter the list.
A bare `@` gives one category overview row (each category name + its count); Enter / the number keys only show a one-line usage hint.
With the default category scope set to “Basic”, untagged entries and entries tagged “Basic” are always shown; an explicit `@category` ignores the scope.
cheat.path.title: File mode #1: type the path directly
cheat.path.summary: A trailing separator = list the whole folder
cheat.path.detail:
Typing an absolute path (`D:\proj\`, `\\srv\share\`) browses that level; with a trailing separator it lists the whole folder, without one you can append a filter word (`D:\proj\rep`).
It does not use the index but reads the disk directly; a path that does not exist yields an empty list and never falls back to ordinary search.
cheat.name_search.title: File mode #2: search by file name
cheat.name_search.summary: Searches the index within the configured scope (default: Desktop/Downloads/Documents)
cheat.name_search.detail:
The apostrophe is followed directly by the word. It may be the ASCII `'`, a curly quote `‘`/`’` (what Chinese IMEs often produce) or the full-width `＇`.
Index scope / depth / cap / rescan interval / min length are all adjustable on the Settings page under “File search”;
defaults: Desktop, Downloads, Documents, depth 4, capped at 30k entries, rescanned every 30 minutes.
At most 30 results. Enter opens it with the associated program; with a folder row selected, Tab enters that folder.
cheat.index_scope.title: File index: scope and timing are configurable
cheat.index_scope.summary: Settings → File search: folders / depth / cap / rescan / min length
cheat.index_scope.detail:
The scan folders default to the three user folders (redirected Desktop and OneDrive locations both count); they can be added or removed and support %ENVVARS%.
Recursion depth 2/4/6/8, entry cap 10k/30k/100k, rescan interval 5–180 minutes, min length for entering file mode 1/2/3.
The exclusion list skips whole folders by name; the seven factory entries such as node_modules / .git can be brought back with “Restore default exclusions”.
After the changes are saved the index is rebuilt in the background automatically; the old index stays usable until the new one is done.
cheat.leading_space.title: File mode #6: leading space
cheat.leading_space.summary: One leading space is the same as entering file mode
cheat.leading_space.detail:
When the query starts with a space the whole string goes to file search, with the same result as `'word`.
How to get the space in: unless “General → Space runs” on the Settings page is on the “Always” tier, Shift+Space always inserts a real space; on the “Always” tier the space key is taken by running,
so Shift+Space is the only way left.
cheat.verbs.title: File mode #3: verb trigger
cheat.verbs.detail:
The three verbs are equivalent and give the same results as `'report`.
When the verb itself is part of a file name it is taken as a word — type one more word and it switches back to an ordinary query.
cheat.types.title: File mode #4: type words
cheat.types.summary: doc / pic / video / audio / zip / exe / cad
cheat.types.detail:
Seven extension categories: `doc` (documents and spreadsheets), `pic` (images), `video`, `audio`, `zip` (archives), `exe` (executables and scripts), `cad` (drawings and models).
Folders are not type-filtered. Arbitrary extension filters such as `ext=pdf` are not implemented (a deviation recorded in the requirement spec).
cheat.folders.title: File mode #5: folders only
cheat.folders.detail: Lists folders only, no files. As with type words, `folder` still needs at least one word after it to enter file mode — typed on its own it may just be the start of some program's name.
cheat.esc_up.title: Folder browsing: back one level at a time
cheat.esc_up.summary: Esc in a folder goes up a level
cheat.esc_up.detail:
Press Esc in folder browsing (`D:\proj\` or `D:\proj\rep`): first it drops the filter words and stays in this folder, press again to go up one level; back at the drive root, the next Esc is what clears the query.
A UNC share root (`\\srv\share\`) is the same as a drive root: there is no browsable folder above it.
In a normal query and in file index search, Esc is still the old "clear the query".
The left side of the status bar says what Esc will do at this moment (go up / clear filter / clear).
cheat.terminal.title: Terminal commands
cheat.terminal.summary: Runs in a new terminal window and stays there when done
cheat.terminal.detail:
`>` is followed directly by the command (no space needed; `> ipconfig` also works); it runs in a new console window, and with `/k` or `-NoExit` ⇒ the output stays in the window.
Typing only `>` (or `> `) just shows a one-line usage hint and runs nothing.
Which shell to use is one of four choices on the Settings page under "Features → Terminal shell": cmd / powershell / pwsh / Windows Terminal.
The raw command never enters the log.
cheat.arrows.title: Select an item
cheat.arrows.summary: Moves the selection between head rows and results
cheat.arrows.detail: ↑↓ only move the selection, they never run anything. No wrap at the top or the bottom.
cheat.insert.title: Mark / unmark
cheat.insert.summary: File rows and file/folder entries can be marked; after marking the selection moves down automatically
cheat.insert.detail:
Press once to add this row to the marked set (a "✓ " appears before the name), press again to remove it; after adding, the selection moves down to the next row automatically, so repeated presses mark a batch in one go (at the last row it stays put and does not wrap to the top).
Only two kinds can be marked: file search rows, and entries in the item list whose type is file / folder. Calculator, terminal, web search, system commands and every kind of hint row refuse the press and only answer with a hint.
The marked set is cleared when the window hides (same rule as the AHK build: the next summon is a clean screen).
With at least one item marked the status bar says "N marked", and pressing → then enters the batch panel.
cheat.paging.title: Paging
cheat.paging.summary: Pages the result list one page; the selection scrolls along
cheat.paging.detail: After paging, the selected item stays inside the visible area (the list scrolls to follow it).
cheat.digits.title: Run by row number
cheat.digits.summary: Runs the first 10 rows; bare keys work only when the input is empty
cheat.digits.detail:
The first 10 rows of the list are numbered at the start of the line; press the matching digit to run that row directly.
Bare digits only work while the query box is empty (with text in it, digits are query content); Ctrl+digit / Alt+digit are not subject to this limit.
Aiming at a row that does not run something (calculator row → copy, hint row → toast) follows that row's own meaning.
cheat.tab.title: Complete / next item
cheat.tab.summary: Switches rule per "Tab key behaviour" on the Settings page
cheat.tab.detail:
In complete-first mode, Tab completes only when exactly one candidate can be extended by this query; otherwise it acts as next item.
When a folder row is selected it always enters that folder (not affected by the Tab mode).
After completing, the caret sits at the end of the query, so you can keep typing without clicking first.
cheat.shift_tab.title: Previous item
cheat.shift_tab.detail: Same as Ctrl+P: cycles to the previous item and is never taken over by completion.
cheat.ctrl_np.title: Next / previous item
cheat.ctrl_np.summary: Always navigation; Ctrl+J / Ctrl+K are another pair
cheat.ctrl_np.detail:
These four keys are always navigation, whatever the Tab mode and the completion result.
The old habits (Ctrl+J / Ctrl+K) are kept and are equivalent to those two.
cheat.space.title: Run the selected item
cheat.space.summary: Four modes: off / full name or alias / single candidate / always
cheat.space.detail:
One of four choices on the Settings page under "General → Run on space", default "Only on the full name": it runs only when the input is empty, or when the whole query exactly equals the selected item's name / alias.
To insert a space in a multi-word query: Shift+Space always inserts a real space (the only way out under the "Always" mode).
With a calculator row / search row selected, Space does not take over (those only accept Enter, clicks and the digit keys).
cheat.enter.title: Run the selected item
cheat.enter.summary: When nothing matches, opens the "add new" dialog
cheat.enter.detail:
Runs the currently selected item; while a modal is open, Enter is that modal's "OK".
When there is not a single result, Enter does not run a command but opens the "add new" dialog prefilled with the current input (revised rule of FR-SRC-23).
cheat.esc.title: Staged back
cheat.esc.summary: In order: close menu → close dialog → exit panel → clear → hide to tray
cheat.esc.detail:
Order: close the ☰ menu → close the advanced page / internal / delete confirmation → close popups and the help page → return from Settings to search → exit the action panel (the original input and selected row are put back) → folder browsing goes up one level → clear the input → hide to tray.
The panel step sitting before "clear the input" is deliberate: when the panel's filter text looks like a path, "go up" or "clear" should not steal it.
The clear step actively takes focus back to the search box (TextEdit drops focus on its own Esc).
cheat.panel.title: Action panel
cheat.panel.summary: → enters the panel; ← / Esc / empty Backspace leaves it
cheat.panel.detail:
With the caret at the end of the input, press → to open the selected item's action panel (holding it down does not keep advancing: only the "new press" counts).
In the panel the input box becomes a filter and the title slot shows the item title inside "Actions for …"; Enter runs the highlighted action,
and with an empty filter the digit keys 1…0 point at the first 10 rows (same rule as result mode). Learning stats are
recorded under the "original query" name, not the action name.
Exiting (← / Esc / Backspace with an empty input) puts the original input text and the selected row back exactly as they were.
Rows that have a panel: list entries, custom command rows, file rows, web search rows, calculator rows (batch E5:
it opens the three-cell "text" table instead, see the "In the panel" entry); terminal / hint rows have nothing to act on,
so → does nothing there (which is also why the status bar's right cell does not light that keycap).
When something is already marked (see the `Insert` entry), → ignores which row is selected and goes straight to the batch panel.
Right-click "Actions…" is the same entry point; the action list is in the next entry.
cheat.panel_actions.title: Actions available
cheat.panel_actions.summary: Given per object: open / elevate / location / copy / paste / properties / Recycle Bin / edit / pin
cheat.panel_actions.detail:
Given by object type, with no buttons that would only throw an error when pressed: open (an entry with run_title uses it as the title),
run as administrator ("No" on UAC counts as cancel, not failure), open with (system dialog),
location (explorer /select), copy path / URL / name, open in terminal (a folder enters this folder,
a file enters its containing folder), properties (the system properties box), move to Recycle Bin (goes to the Recycle Bin, does not delete the list entry),
edit / add as command, delete (still asks for confirmation once more), pin / unpin, large-type display.
Batch E6 (2026-10-27) adds the two single-row cells the original text owed: copy file / cut file — offered only when
something really exists on disk (the same gate as properties and Recycle Bin); what goes to the clipboard is a file object Explorer recognizes,
the same payload as those two entries in the batch panel, except that here there is only this one path.
`shell:` named items and `internal:` action rows get only the "open / copy / edit / large-type" half;
properties, location, terminal and Recycle Bin do not appear — they have nothing to work on for an object with no on-disk path.
A calculator row is a string of text, not something on a disk ⇒ it has a separate three-cell table: copy this string (what Enter normally
does) / paste into the previous window / large-type display, with no "open" — handing 14 to the system to search
looks for a program called "14".
After it finishes: open / elevate / terminal / location / paste succeeded ⇒ the window goes to the tray; edit / delete /
add as command / Recycle Bin succeeded ⇒ the panel exits back to results; copy / properties / open with / large-type ⇒ the panel stays where it is.
cheat.batch_panel.title: Batch panel
cheat.batch_panel.summary: Seven actions: open all / copy / cut / copy paths / copy to / add as commands / Recycle Bin
cheat.batch_panel.detail:
With something marked, → ignores which row is currently selected and opens the panel for the marked set, with the title slot reading "N marked". The filter, Enter and the digit keys in the panel are the same set as in the single-entry panel. Seven actions:
· Open all: launches them one by one in marking order; on success the panel closes and the window goes to the tray; if not a single one opened it stays put and answers with one line.
· Copy files / cut files: written as a file object Explorer recognizes (CF_HDROP); cut additionally writes Preferred DropEffect, so pasting elsewhere moves them. Pasting does not clear the marks for you.
· Copy all paths: one per line, Windows line breaks.
· Copy to…: first a system folder picker appears, then they are copied one by one; a same-named file at the target is left to the system to ask about overwriting. A source that is exactly the target folder or beneath it is skipped (a folder is never copied into itself).
· Add all as commands: builds custom commands from the entry names, skips ones already pointing at the same path, and merges the new ones into the list, persisting to disk immediately.
· All to Recycle Bin: first a confirmation box appears (Enter runs / Esc cancels). They are moved one by one; if the system's "permanently delete" warning gets "No" for one item, that item counts as cancelled and does not affect the rest; when done the panel retracts and the marks are cleared.
The marked set only ever holds files and folders, so all seven actions apply to every item and no per-item trimming is done.
cheat.secondary.title: Secondary action
cheat.secondary.summary: Shortcut mode by default: locate file rows / copy web row URLs / paste for calculator rows; rebindable, switchable to panel mode
cheat.secondary.detail:
Performs a "secondary action" on the selected row — Enter opens it; this key does something else.
The Settings page's Hotkeys page has two forms (shortcut mode by default, switchable at any time):
· Shortcut mode: file row / folder row "locate in Explorer", web search row "copy URL",
calculator row "paste into the window that was in front before summoning" (typing only, your clipboard untouched);
app entries, system commands and custom commands have no "obviously it" secondary action ⇒ it only hints that you press →
to see everything, and does not guess for you (deliberately no "open" either: Enter already opens).
· Panel mode: same as moving that → entry onto this key — the action goes to the panel and you pick there.
How "paste into the original window" avoids pasting in the wrong place: at summon time it first records who the foreground window was,
and before pasting it passes three gates — that window is still open, the system is willing to give it focus, and the focus really is there at that moment.
If any one fails, not a single character is sent, only one sentence saying why; the send goes through the typing channel, not the clipboard.
This key only works on the search page, with no dialog open and no panel open; it is not registered with the system, so it steals no keys from
other programs and is never swallowed wholesale by the system like a global summon key. It must include Ctrl or Alt (bare keys and Shift-only
keys are just typing), and Win combos cannot be set; the key itself can be recorded on the same page and restored to default (Backspace /
Delete), and a change takes effect at once and is written to settings.json.
While the add/edit dialog is open, this key does "test run" inside the dialog instead — it launches once from the current form,
the window is not closed, and no usage statistics are recorded (batch D4, see the Ctrl+O entry).
cheat.pick_file.title: Dialog · Pick file
cheat.pick_file.summary: Only inside the add/edit dialog: command line = the chosen file, alias / name derived from the file name
cheat.pick_file.detail:
For filling in a path in the add/edit dialog (requirement spec FR-CFG-06); on the search page this key does nothing else.
Opens the system file picker, which can only choose files that already exist — avoiding a hand-typed name that does not. After you pick:
· Command line = the full path of that file;
· alias / name is derived from the file name the way Delphi ALTRun's `btnFileClick` does: strip the last extension segment,
and anything starting with `//` is treated as a URL (that is how Chrome `--app=…` command lines become host names).
If those two fields already hold other values ⇒ it first asks "Replace / Keep"; with "Keep" only the empty fields are filled in,
the command line is replaced all the same (that is what this command actually is). While the question is open, Esc only dismisses the question and does not close the dialog.
You can also skip the key and drag a .lnk / program / folder straight into the dialog (same as Delphi's `WM_DropFiles`):
a .lnk is dereferenced to the target it points at, while a .lnk pointing at the system Installer cache folder is imported as the .lnk itself.
For system commands (`internal:<id>`) the whole group of buttons and hotkeys is unavailable — once the command line is overwritten it can no longer run.
cheat.pick_dir.title: Dialog · Pick folder
cheat.pick_dir.summary: Only inside the add/edit dialog: command line = the chosen folder, name taken from the folder's last segment
cheat.pick_dir.detail:
Same path as `Ctrl+O`, except it picks a folder (the same system picker, switched to the folder-selection form).
Command line = the folder's full path; alias / name takes the segment after the last `\`, without stripping an extension —
dot-containing folder names like `1.2images` are kept as-is (on this branch Delphi checks `DirectoryExists` first).
The type becomes "Folder" as well. Same again: if those two fields already hold other values it asks "Replace / Keep" first, and Esc only dismisses the question.
cheat.new_item.title: New shortcut
cheat.new_item.summary: Prefills this row when a file row is selected
cheat.new_item.detail:
Opens the "New" dialog; when the selected row is a file search row, that row's path and type are prefilled.
When the current input is not empty, the current input is prefilled instead (the same entry as Enter when nothing matches).
cheat.edit.title: Edit selected item
cheat.edit.detail:
Edits that entry in the item list. A file search row is not in the list, so this does not apply to it (for such a row, "add as shortcut" is what makes sense).
Built-in commands (the system commands group) have a read-only type, so how they run cannot be changed.
`F3` is an alias added in batch B8 (2026-10-26, requirement spec appendix A) and takes exactly the same path as `Ctrl+E`;
while the action panel is open neither takes over (same rule as `Insert`).
cheat.delete.title: Delete selected item
cheat.delete.summary: Both ask for confirmation; Delete works only when the input is empty
cheat.delete.detail:
Removes from the item list; files on disk are not deleted. Both keys mean the same thing, only their availability differs:
Delete works only when the search box is empty (with text in it, the Delete key has to delete characters); Ctrl+Shift+D works whether or not there is text.
cheat.open_dir.title: Open containing folder
cheat.open_dir.summary: List item = open its folder; file row = reveal it
cheat.open_dir.detail:
List item: opens its containing folder in Explorer.
File search row: reveals and selects this file in Explorer.
The right-click menu has the same thing (file rows).
cheat.pin.title: Pin / unpin
cheat.pin.summary: Pinned items carry a badge at the icon's top-right
cheat.pin.detail:
Toggles the selected item's pin state and gives a one-line toast in reply, persisting to disk immediately.
A pin only overrides the order within the same match tier; it never makes a more precise hit give way.
The right-click menu has the same thing.
cheat.file_mode.title: Enter file mode
cheat.file_mode.summary: Prepends a `'` trigger to the input
cheat.file_mode.detail: When already in file mode it only gives a one-line hint and does not stack a second prefix.
cheat.import_all.title: Batch import all
cheat.import_all.summary: Scans the Start menu in the background and merges the results into the list
cheat.import_all.detail:
Merges the Start menu's shortcuts into the list in one go (deduplicated by uid; existing items are not added again).
The tray menu has the same thing.
cheat.scope_toggle.title: Toggle default category scope
cheat.scope_toggle.summary: All ⇄ Basic, the list follows immediately
cheat.scope_toggle.detail:
Switches between "All" (every entry joins the candidate pool) and "Basic" (untagged ∪ tagged "Basic"),
which is the same setting as "General → Default category scope" on the Settings page; after switching it writes to disk at once and shows a one-line toast.
An explicit `@category` filter is not affected by this setting.
cheat.hide.title: Hide selected item
cheat.hide.summary: Factory / scanned / custom entries all work; restore under Settings → Advanced
cheat.hide.detail:
Writes the selected entry into `hidden[]` and drops it from the list, while also storing a full snapshot in settings.json;
no files on disk are deleted, and no other fields of the entry are removed.
Works only when the search box is empty — with text in it, Ctrl+Del is the input box's "delete the next word".
Neither a rescan nor "restore missing built-in commands" puts it back; after restoring, the pin and the learned counts come back with it.
To delete it for good, use Delete / Ctrl+Shift+D (which asks for confirmation).
Restore entry point: Settings → Advanced → "Hidden items".
cheat.large_type.title: Large-type display
cheat.large_type.summary: Enlarges the selected row to the center of the screen; with no selected row it shows the raw input
cheat.large_type.detail:
Borderless and always on top, `141414` black with white text (not following the theme), the window centered in the workspace.
Font size steps by character count: ≤12 → 96, ≤30 → 64, ≤80 → 40, ≤300 → 28, anything else 18;
if it does not fit on screen it keeps stepping down, and the window size never exceeds the workspace.
The main window stays where it is with the large type on top of it; after closing it, focus returns to the main window and you can keep editing the query.
To close: Esc / one click / switching to another window. The displayed content is never logged.
cheat.copy_line.title: Copy this row
cheat.copy_line.summary: Path for files, number for the calculator, name for apps; does not close the window
cheat.copy_line.detail:
It copies the "copyable content" of the currently highlighted row, the same string as the `Ctrl+L` large-type display (batch B8, 2026-10-26):
file / folder / web search rows take the path or URL, a calculator row takes the computed number,
apps and commands in the list take the name, and a parameter hint row takes the command text.
When the search box has focus and text is selected, this key yields to the input box — what is copied is the text you selected, not the list row.
After copying, the window stays put (the AHK build closed on copy; this one does not, so you can press Ctrl+V next).
When this screen has no copyable row it only gives a one-line hint. Copied content is never logged, only the character count.
cheat.alt_enter.title: Copy this row (another key)
cheat.alt_enter.summary: The same string as Ctrl+C; while the panel is open it is Enter
cheat.alt_enter.detail:
Batch E6 (2026-10-27, the last cell of requirement spec FR-ACT-01): `Alt+Enter` copies the currently highlighted row,
taking exactly the same string as `Ctrl+C` (in the AHK build those two keys were the same `CopyText()`).
When the search box has focus and text is selected it likewise yields to the input box and copies the text you selected.
While the action panel is open this key does not take over: Enter in the panel means "run the highlighted action",
and adding Alt on top does not change that (same rule as AHK's `_Execute`).
It is an in-window hotkey and is not registered with the system ⇒ Alt+Enter in other programs (properties dialogs and the like) is unaffected;
for the same reason neither the summon key nor the secondary action key may be recorded as this combo (the `? hotkeys` page blocks it).
After copying the window is not closed, the content is not logged, only the character count.
cheat.history.title: Browse search history
cheat.history.summary: Recalls a previously run string; it only fills in the text and does not run it for you
cheat.history.detail:
Batch C3 (2026-10-26, requirement spec FR-QRY-10): `Ctrl+↑` goes one entry further back, `Ctrl+↓` one entry newer.
At the oldest it simply stops there (the input box does not move); once at the newest, pressing `Ctrl+↓` again returns to the string you just typed.
What goes into history is "the string that was submitted": Enter to launch, clicking a file row, a `>` terminal command, copying from the calculator,
picking a row in the panel and leaving — each counts as one run. A failed launch is recorded too (AHK's `Knowledge.Record` books it before running as well;
what you want is to change two characters and try again, so the string in the box has to stay).
Only text is stored, never results: a recalled string still needs Enter to run, and it never selects any row for you.
Duplicates match case-insensitively (`C:\Foo` and `c:\foo` are the same), but are stored as typed, without changing case.
The limit and "stop recording" live in the "Search history" cell on the General page; to wipe it clean right now, use the button on the Advanced page.
It does not take over while the action panel is open or in file mode (the ' and > forms): there ↑↓ are their own navigation keys.
Bare `↑` `↓` still select entries, and adding Shift (`Ctrl+Shift+↑`) still counts as browsing history.
cheat.param_box.title: Fill parameters first, then run
cheat.param_box.summary: When encoding ≠ no parameters and the entry has {%p} (or no marker at all), this box appears before Enter
cheat.param_box.detail:
Batch B6 (2026-10-28, requirement spec FR-ACT-07): pressing Enter to run a matched parameterized item first brings up the parameter box, and you press Enter once more after filling it in to actually launch; Esc cancels and nothing starts.
Only `{%p}` (or "encoding ≠ no parameters yet not a single marker") brings up the box; entries that only use on-the-spot markers such as `{%c}` / `{%wt}` start directly.
Under the box is a list of "recently used parameters"; click one to fill it into the input box. That table is `param_history.json`, and confirming in the box with a non-empty value records one entry (a failed launch is recorded too). The order is the order in the file (newest first), and reusing the same value only bumps its count without moving it; at most 50 entries, and when that is exceeded the least-used one is deleted (ties delete the later one).
Only the string you typed into this box by hand enters history; on-the-spot values such as the clipboard or window titles are not stored, and the raw parameter text is not logged either.
The clear entry point is "Clear parameter history" on the Advanced page (no backup is written for this one).
This box does not change the entry itself; encoding and the way markers are written are edited in the edit dialog (Ctrl+E).
cheat.about.title: About this program
cheat.about.summary: Version, program location, item count; Esc closes
cheat.about.detail:
The dialog shows the version number, the exe path, the current number of entries in the list, and a note that “the log does not record the raw text from the query box”.
Added in batch B8 (2026-10-26, requirement spec appendix A); like `F2` it is “whole-window level”,
so it still works while the Settings page is open. It is not in the ☰ menu, and not in the tray menu either.
Close: Esc or click “Close (Esc)”; after closing, focus returns to the search box.
cheat.config_dir.title: Open the config folder
cheat.config_dir.summary: Opens the config folder in Explorer (not a single file)
cheat.config_dir.detail:
The requirement spec appendix A literally says “open the config file”; what opens here is that folder:
the folder holds `settings.json`, `user_items.json` and `launcher.log` at the same time,
so pointing at any one file has no unique answer, hence the folder (deviation logged in batch B8).
When the list folder is writable it sits next to the exe, otherwise it falls back to `%LOCALAPPDATA%` — either way the one actually in use is opened.
It is independent of the selected row and also works while the action panel is open. If the folder does not exist you get a one-line notice.
cheat.ctrl_backspace.title: Delete the previous word in the input box
cheat.ctrl_backspace.summary: Built into egui's input box; this program does not take over this key
cheat.ctrl_backspace.detail:
With the caret in the search box, `Ctrl+Backspace` deletes the previous word, or the selection if there is one —
this part is done by egui's own TextEdit; this program does not register that key.
The counterpart `Ctrl+Del` deletes the next word, but with an empty input box `Ctrl+Del` means “hide the selected item”.
“Backspace on an empty filter = leave the action panel” only honours the unmodified press (a real-machine test on the same day as batch B8 caught
`Ctrl+Backspace` closing the panel along with it; that was changed to read the modifiers carried by the event).
cheat.settings_page.title: Open / return from the Settings page
cheat.settings_page.summary: Nine pages: General / Features / Hotkeys / Sources / File search / Appearance / Advanced / Batch manage / Usage
cheat.menu.title: Main menu
cheat.menu.summary: New, batch import, settings, cheat sheet, open log, exit
cheat.menu.detail:
The three bars at the top right of the title bar. Batch F6 (2026-10-24) used it to replace the “＋ New” button next to the input box,
and the first item in the menu is New; the Ctrl+Shift+N path is still there as before.
Esc only dismisses the menu (it does not clear the input or close the window); clicking anywhere outside the menu dismisses it too.
As soon as the window hides, the menu state is not kept.
cheat.manage.title: Batch manage
cheat.manage.summary: Settings page 8: tick to delete in bulk, select broken only, absolute ↔ relative path conversion
cheat.manage.detail:
Opens the Settings page's “Batch manage” directly (the last item in the left category bar; going in from the Settings page is the same).
Once entries are ticked you can: convert to the relative form (`%LAUNCHER_DIR%\…`, only rows under this program's folder), restore to an absolute path,
or delete them from the list. Deleting only touches `user_items.json` and never files on disk; converting only changes the command-line field, parameters and working directory stay untouched.
The state column uses the same four states as the main screen: “Select broken only” ticks only `Not found`; `Offline` (an unplugged USB stick / a dropped share) does not count as broken.
Both batch actions ask for confirmation first, and the confirmation box states the number of rows. The requirement spec's portable form is `.\`; this repo uses `%LAUNCHER_DIR%`
instead (`.\` resolves against the process's current directory, and this program never calls SetCurrentDirectory, so the same list would work sometimes and not others).
cheat.manage_recheck.title: Batch manage · Re-check
cheat.manage_recheck.summary: Only works on the Settings page's “Batch manage”
cheat.manage_recheck.detail:
Runs the four-state path check again and the state column refreshes at once (entering this page also runs a round automatically).
If the previous round has not returned it does not stack threads: a disconnected network drive can make the check hang for a long time, so pressing it then only tells you to wait.
cheat.usage.title: Usage
cheat.usage.summary: Settings page 9: total / last-30-day bars / count by feature / top 10 items
cheat.usage.detail:
Opens the Settings page's “Usage” directly (left category bar; since batch D2 one more page, “Web engines”, follows it). This page is a read-only dashboard: apart from “Clear statistics” there is nothing you can change.
The total and the “count by feature” data live in `usage.json`: only which day, which kind of feature and how many times are recorded; query text / item names / paths never enter this file.
The counting points are the same set as the per-item cumulative counts: a list item and a system command each count once when they run successfully; a successful calculator copy, a web search,
files and folders, terminal commands and custom commands opening successfully likewise; anything that did not run is not counted.
The “cumulative count / last used” on an item is a separate ledger (used for ranking), and clearing statistics does not touch it — to clear that one, use “Reset learning order”.
Kept for 400 days (including today): anything older is trimmed by real date, and date keys that cannot be parsed are dropped outright.
A single launch can land in both the “list item” and the “custom command” buckets (this list entry was launched / a custom command was executed),
so the total can exceed the actual number of launches — this is an intentional convention, not double counting (kept by the user's ruling on 2026-10-29).
cheat.web_engines.title: Web engines table
cheat.web_engines.summary: Settings page 10: add, edit and delete search engines, pick the fallback engine
cheat.web_engines.detail:
Opens the Settings page's “Web engines” directly (left category bar).
Each row is “keyword / name / URL template”: only keyword + space + term takes over the whole list, and {query} in the template is replaced by the term.
Edit a field and click elsewhere to save; “Restore the nine factory engines” swaps the whole table back to the nine factory ones, and engines you added are wiped.
“Fallback search” decides which engine produces a row when there are no results at all; the factory setting is Google → Bing.
Rows missing a keyword or a URL, and rows whose keyword repeats an earlier one, are not saved when you leave this page (the page warns with the row count first).
cheat.global_hotkey.title: Global hotkey
cheat.global_hotkey.summary: Factory Ctrl+Alt+Space; both can be changed on the Settings page
cheat.global_hotkey.detail:
The summon key is recorded on the Settings page's “Hotkeys” page; the factory setting is Ctrl+Alt+Space.
When the summon key is a bare key (such as `` ` ``), that one character can no longer be typed anywhere system-wide ⇒ pair it with a “type-back key” on the same page to type the character back into the focused window; when the summon key has a modifier, the type-back key does nothing when pressed.
If another program owns the hotkey, registration fails and the Settings page leaves a note behind.
cheat.extra_hotkey.title: Secondary summon hotkey
cheat.extra_hotkey.summary: A second summon key with the same effect as the main one; editable and clearable on the Settings page
cheat.extra_hotkey.detail:
Ships as Alt+R (the AHK build's “secondary hotkey”). On the Settings page's “Hotkeys” page you can record a new combo or clear it — once cleared only the main summon key remains.
Same rules as the main summon key: a modifier is required, and it must not be the same combo as the main summon key or the type-back key; settings.json is written only after a successful registration, and a failure reports the error as it is and puts the previous key back.
cheat.dbltap.title: Double-tap summon
cheat.dbltap.summary: Tap the same modifier twice to toggle show/hide once (off by default)
cheat.dbltap.detail:
Three options on the Settings page's “Hotkeys” page: Off / Double-tap Ctrl / Double-tap Shift; the factory setting is Off.
The rule follows the AHK build: only two taps within 400ms count as a double tap; holding one down for over 300ms does not count (that is the start of a combo such as Ctrl+C); if the gap between the two releases is under 25ms it is discarded as remote-control software / automation jitter. Left and right Ctrl / Shift both count, and the two taps may be different sides.
When on, this program installs a “listen-only, never blocking” keyboard hook: every key still reaches the program you are using as usual, and the hook only counts the two taps. Combos such as Shift+CapsLock work as usual.
cheat.selection_panel.title: Selection action panel
cheat.selection_panel.summary: Takes whatever is selected in the foreground window straight into the action panel
cheat.selection_panel.detail:
Ships as Ctrl+Alt+\ (the AHK build's feature of the same name). On the Settings page's “Hotkeys” page you can record a new combo or clear it.
The capture follows the AHK build's old routine: first take an all-format snapshot of the clipboard and empty it, then send Ctrl+C to the foreground window (Ctrl+Insert for console-type windows), waiting at most 0.8 seconds; once something is captured, put the snapshot back verbatim — whatever you had copied to the clipboard before is still there, images and file objects included.
When the hotkey includes Alt, holding it down would turn the copy key into a combo, so the program waits until you release the modifiers before sending.
A single file / folder captured ⇒ actions like open, show location, copy path; several ⇒ the batch panel;
a URL ⇒ the search row's action set; plain text ⇒ copy, type into the window that was active before summon (without touching the clipboard), large-type display.
When nothing is captured it only shows a notice and does not open the main window. When the main window has the Settings page or a dialog open it does not show the panel,
and instead tells you to close it and press the key again — the captured content will not discard the input you are editing.
cheat.move_window.title: Move the window
cheat.move_window.summary: Empty title-bar space or empty space right of the list
cheat.move_window.detail:
The roughly 20px strip between the search box and ☰ in the title bar, the empty space right of the settings title, and the empty space right of the list can all be dragged.
The middle button no longer runs any entry (deprecated 2026-10-18).
cheat.wheel.title: Move the selection
cheat.wheel.summary: One notch, one row; stops at the top and bottom without wrapping
cheat.wheel.detail:
Batch B8 (2026-10-26, requirement spec appendix A “wheel moves the selection”, same rule as the AHK build):
one wheel notch on the result list = the selection moves up or down one row, with exactly the same boundaries as ↑↓ (no wrap-around).
The list position is not scrolled separately; the existing “scroll follows selection” still handles that, so the following rows stay visible as usual.
One notch moves exactly one row — it never moves the selection and scrolls a stretch at the same time; both places use the same criterion.
For fast movement there is PgUp / PgDn (a whole page). A wheel turn with a modifier does not move the selection.
While the add/edit dialog, delete confirmation, batch confirmation, About page or help page is on top,
the wheel falls back to its default behaviour: it only scrolls the list and leaves the selection alone.
cheat.resize.title: Resize the window
cheat.resize.summary: 6px invisible handles on four edges and four corners; one keyboard step is 60×40
cheat.resize.detail:
Mouse: left-drag any of the four edges or four corners (each a 6px invisible handle), minimum 360×240.
Keyboard: Ctrl+= grows, Ctrl+- shrinks, one step is 60×40 logical pixels, up to 1200×900.
The window size is only remembered for the current run; quitting the program returns to the default size.
cheat.row_density.title: Row tightness and window height
cheat.row_density.summary: A · Snug (default) / B · Roomy / C · Ultra-dense / Follow theme
cheat.row_density.detail:
Settings page “General → List row density” (batch F6, 2026-10-24, from you: “the overall UI height is too tall,
the gaps between items are too large”, and you asked for the three steps to be options, A by default).
A = row height 34 / icon 24 / gap 2 ⇒ window height 438; B = 40 / 28 / 2 ⇒ 498;
C = 24 / 16 / 0 ⇒ 318; Follow theme = back to the theme JSON's row_height and icon_size.
All four modes keep “exactly ten rows on screen”: switching recomputes the window height from the new row height at once, the width stays put.
Outside the “Follow theme” mode, these two theme keys take no part in rendering (the other keys still apply as usual).
Those totals assume the Light padding of 14; another theme only differs by those few padding pixels.
The input row is not affected by row density: its height is fixed at 44, and the font size still follows the theme's “input font size”.

destructive.learning.title: Reset learning?
destructive.learning.warning: Clears every entry's use count and last-used time: ranking returns to the no-Boost state; pins are kept. Learned aliases remain (indistinguishable from hand-typed ones). user_items.json is backed up before writing.
destructive.restore.title: Restore defaults?
destructive.restore.warning: Resets Space-to-run / Tab behavior / learning order / data sources / dangerous-action confirmation / terminal shell / theme / visible rows / row density / default scope / history limit. Hotkeys, web engines, hidden entries, custom commands and pins are kept. settings.json is backed up before writing.
destructive.history.title: Clear search history?
destructive.history.warning: Empties search_history.json: Ctrl+↑ starts from an empty table and the strings you typed can no longer be recalled. The history-limit setting is unchanged. No backup is written for this one (the other two buttons back up because they clear statistics; this table holds the raw text).
destructive.usage.title: Clear usage statistics?
destructive.usage.warning: Empties usage.json: totals, the last-30-days bars and the per-feature counts all go to zero. Per-entry use counts and last-used times are kept (they drive ranking; clear those with "Reset learning"). No backup is written for this one.
destructive.param.title: Clear parameter history?
destructive.param.warning: Empties param_history.json: the "recently used parameters" list under the parameter box of marked entries becomes empty. No backup is written for this one.

hotkey.err.typeback_needs_mod: The type-back hotkey needs a modifier; a bare one would swallow the character itself

hotkey.err.extra_needs_mod: The secondary summon hotkey needs a modifier; a bare key would be swallowed system-wide
hotkey.err.extra_same_as_toggle: The secondary summon hotkey cannot equal the summon hotkey; the system would treat it as summon
hotkey.err.extra_same_as_typeback: The secondary summon hotkey cannot equal the type-back hotkey; only the first registration wins
hotkey.err.selection_needs_mod: The selection hotkey needs a modifier; a bare key would be swallowed system-wide
hotkey.err.selection_same_as_toggle: The selection hotkey cannot equal the summon hotkey; the system would treat it as summon
hotkey.err.selection_same_as_typeback: The selection hotkey cannot equal the type-back hotkey; only the first registration wins
hotkey.err.selection_same_as_extra: The selection hotkey cannot equal the secondary summon hotkey; only the first registration wins
hotkey.err.secondary_no_win: In-window hotkeys cannot use Win: egui does not pass Win on Windows, so it would never match
hotkey.err.secondary_need_ctrl_alt: In-window hotkeys need Ctrl or Alt; bare and Shift-only keys are just typing and would be lost
hotkey.err.secondary_same_as_toggle: Cannot equal the global summon hotkey; that chord is swallowed system-wide and never reaches the window
hotkey.err.secondary_same_as_typeback: Cannot equal the type-back hotkey; that key is reserved for giving the character back
